decisive_items: Brain MRI showed a recent ischemic infarction in the left paramedian medulla without hemorrhagic transformation;
A 36‐year‐old man of Indian origin presented at 2:30 a.m. with acute right‐sided weakness and three episodes of vomiting.
Noncontrast CT of the head showed no acute pathology but revealed an incidental 4 × 6 mm hyperdense focus in the left parasagittal frontal cortex suggestive of a cavernoma.
response.rationale: The acute presentation and MRI-confirmed recent ischemic infarction in the left paramedian medulla establish ischemic stroke as the diagnosis; the frontal cavernoma is an incidental finding unrelated to the acute brainstem infarct.

rejected.why: The cavernoma is described as incidental and located in the frontal cortex, whereas the acute symptoms and imaging localize to the left paramedian medullary infarction, making it an unlikely cause of the presenting stroke.
